verdict.rationale: DBOS documents starting workflows in the background with `DBOS.start_workflow`, which returns handles you can wait on for results. It also documents queues that run many workflows at once with managed concurrency. Together these give a documented basis for child workflows and fan-out/fan-in. However, the evidence never explicitly describes parallel steps within a workflow, fan-out over dynamically sized batches, or a fan-in pattern, so composition is only implied. missing for 10: explicit parallel-step execution docs, documented dynamic-batch fan-out/fan-in pattern, explicit child-workflow (parent/child) semantics, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a backend developer, I compose workflows from parallel steps, fan-out/fan-in over dynamic batches, and child workflows without hand-rolling coordination

citations.quote: You can use DBOS.start_workflow to start a workflow in the background. If you start a workflow this way, it returns a workflow handle, from which you can access information about the workflow or wait for it to complete and retrieve its result.
You can use queues to run many workflows at once with managed concurrency.
Because every task is checkpointed, your agent can recover from any failure mid-flight without re-running work that already succeeded.
